These are balance-sheet recognition events, not earning power. Using the 21.0 percent US federal statutory rate as the going-forward assumption. The FY2025 figure was computed by hand from the disclosed provision and pre-tax income and does not change the conclusion, but the decision was taken against a partial list.

Restricted cash of 2,542 is excluded because it is not available to service debt; it is disclosed as two lines, current 631 and non-current 1,911, which is the same current-plus-non-current combination the UBER_FY2024 override already made by hand for its 2,717. effective_tax_rate.rationale: Same policy as UBER_FY2024. Reported rates are distorted by one-off deferred tax events: FY2025 shows a 2,897,255 thousand tax benefit against a pre-tax LOSS of 53,247 thousand, an effective rate of 5441.2 percent, while FY2023 to FY2024 swing from -2.6 to 10.1 percent. The 2,897,255 benefit is 102 percent of reported net income of 2,844,008 and is a balance-sheet recognition event, not earning power. Using the 21.0 percent US federal statutory rate as the going-forward assumption, identical to UBER_FY2024 so the two valuations stay comparable. KNOWN DIRECTIONAL ASSUMPTION: large loss carryforwards mean the near-term CASH tax rate is likely well below 21 percent, so this understates value.

net_debt.rationale: Same policy as UBER_FY2024. Long-term debt net of current portion 1,002,404 less cash and cash equivalents 1,132,009 less short-term investments 705,172, all in USD thousands as reported, giving net CASH of 834,777 thousand. Restricted cash of 705,361 is excluded because it is not available to service debt. Operating lease liabilities are excluded because their cost already sits inside operating cash flow. Unlike UBER_FY2024 the current portion is not a gap: convertible senior notes, current are nil at FY2025 against 390,175 at FY2024, so no current debt is omitted.

revenue_growth.rationale: FY2024 growth of 31.4 percent and FY2025 of 9.2 percent are not draws from one distribution: Lyft moved from a mature North American ridesharing market to international expansion, acquiring Freenow in July 2025 and TBR in October 2025. Averaging them would restate the dispersion the gate correctly refused. Using the FY2025 rate of 9.2 percent as the going-forward year-one assumption. THIS IS TOTAL GROWTH, NOT ORGANIC: 9.2 percent already contains roughly half a year of Freenow and one quarter of TBR, so organic growth was lower and cannot be quantified from the filing alone. It is also directionally CONSERVATIVE for FY2026, which carries a full year of both: reported Q2 2026 revenue growth was 16.1 percent and sell-side consensus for FY2026 is about 15 percent. Those figures are deliberately excluded from the base case because the other filers derive their growth from the filing, and importing a consensus forecast for one company and not the others would make the cross-company comparison measure the input source rather than the businesses. The consensus path belongs in sensitivity, and the reverse DCF reports what the market price implies.

effective_tax_rate.rationale: Same 21.0 percent US federal statutory policy as the other two filers, so the three valuations stay comparable, but for a different reason than theirs. Uber's and Lyft's reported rates are distorted by one-off valuation allowance releases; DoorDash's are distorted by a company crossing into profitability, with rates of -5.8 percent in FY2023, 25.0 percent in FY2024 and 0.7 percent in FY2025. A summary statistic over a loss year, a first profitable year and a year of loss carryforward utilisation describes a transition, not a going-forward rate. KNOWN DIRECTIONAL ASSUMPTION: remaining carryforwards mean the near-term CASH tax rate is likely below 21 percent, so this understates value.

net_debt.rationale: Same policy as the other two filers. Convertible notes, net 2,724 less cash and cash equivalents 4,378 less short-term investments 1,128, giving net CASH of 2,782. Restricted cash of 273 is excluded because it is not available to service debt. Operating lease liabilities are excluded because their cost already sits inside operating cash flow. The component list printed under the block was verified complete for this filing, with no unmatched-fact line, unlike DASH_FY2024 which prints its short-term securities under a different caption (see ISSUES.md #26). Convertible notes are DoorDash's first balance-sheet debt: 2,750 principal issued May 2025, carried net of 26 in unamortised issuance costs.

interest_expense.rationale: DoorDash has no interest expense to add back. Its income statement reports only Interest income, net, with no gross interest expense line, and its only debt is the 2030 Convertible Notes, which Note 9 states do not bear regular cash interest. The 0.22 percent effective rate disclosed there is the amortisation of 26 of issuance costs over the note's life, an accounting charge already inside operating cash flow, not a cash coupon. Additional interest can accrue only on specific default-type events capped at 0.50 percent, none of which had occurred at 31 December 2025. Set to zero rather than to an estimate: no dollar interest expense is disclosed anywhere in the filing, and inventing one to fill the FCFF formula's interest term would be a fabricated input. The block was correct; it reflected an absence in the company, not a failure of extraction.
